title: Singhasari
capsule: The Singhasari kingdom was a Javanese Hindu-Buddhist polity founded in 1222 by Ken Arok after his defeat of the last Kediri king Kertajaya at the Battle of Ganter, with its capital at Tumapel near present-day Malang in East Java. Under its fifth and final ruler Kertanegara (r. 1268–1292), Singhasari pursued an expansionist maritime policy, sending naval expeditions to Sumatra, Bali, and Malaya and mutilating Kublai Khan's envoy in 1289—a provocative act that triggered a Mongol invasion fleet. In 1292, while Kertanegara's forces were campaigning abroad, the vassal lord Jayakatwang of Kediri sacked the capital and killed the king; the Mongol fleet arrived in 1293 only to be outmaneuvered by Kertanegara's son-in-law Raden Wijaya, who used the Mongols against Jayakatwang and then turned on them to found the Majapahit Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core territory in eastern Java is established through the Pararaton chronicle and numerous dated stone inscriptions; the outer limits of its claimed sovereignty over tributary states in the archipelago are less precisely mapped.
